mcq.q: How can a child trust God when facing a challenge?
options: Pray, read the Bible and ask for help from trusted people
mcq.explanation: Trust in God shows in prayer and seeking help.

mcq.q: What does it mean to acknowledge God's power?
options: To admit that our strength comes from Him and thank Him
mcq.explanation: Acknowledging means to accept and thank.

mcq.q: Who had the dreams about seven cows and seven heads of grain?
mcq.explanation: Genesis 41 says that Pharaoh had the dreams.

mcq.q: Who first told Pharaoh about Joseph?
mcq.explanation: The cupbearer remembered Joseph from prison.

mcq.q: What did the seven fat cows stand for?
mcq.explanation: Joseph explained that they were seven good years.

mcq.q: What did the seven thin cows stand for?
mcq.explanation: The thin cows were seven years of famine.

mcq.q: Whom did Joseph credit for the interpretation?
mcq.explanation: Joseph said, "God will give Pharaoh the answer."

mcq.q: What did Joseph advise Pharaoh to store during the good years?
mcq.explanation: Genesis 41:34 says to take a fifth.

mcq.q: What position did Pharaoh give Joseph?
mcq.explanation: Joseph was put in charge of Egypt, next to Pharaoh.

mcq.q: Which verse says that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge?
mcq.explanation: Proverbs 1:7 says this.

mcq.q: What does it mean to fear God?
options: To respect and love Him and obey Him
mcq.explanation: The fear of God is deep respect.

mcq.q: What is a famine?
options: A long time when there is not enough food
mcq.explanation: A famine is a serious shortage of food.

mcq.q: What lesson can we learn from Joseph's plan?
options: Plan and save for hard times
mcq.explanation: Joseph advised saving in good years.

mcq.q: Where was Joseph when the cupbearer remembered him?
mcq.explanation: Joseph was in prison in Egypt.

mcq.q: Why is Joseph a good example of leadership?
options: He was honest, wise and hardworking
mcq.explanation: These qualities helped him to lead Egypt well.

mcq.q: Which city did Abram come from?
mcq.explanation: Abram was born in Ur of the Chaldeans.

mcq.q: Where did Abram live before going to Canaan?
mcq.explanation: Terah's family settled in Haran.

mcq.q: What did God tell Abram to do?
options: Leave his country and go to a land God would show him
mcq.explanation: Genesis 12:1 records the call.

mcq.q: How old was Abram when he left Haran?
mcq.explanation: Genesis 12:4 says he was seventy-five.

mcq.q: Who went with Abram to Canaan?
mcq.explanation: Sarai his wife and Lot his nephew went with him.

mcq.q: What was Abram's name changed to?
mcq.explanation: Genesis 17:5 records the new name.

mcq.q: What does the name Abraham point to?
mcq.explanation: God said that he would be a father of many nations.

mcq.q: How old was Abram when God changed his name?
mcq.explanation: Genesis 17:1 says he was ninety-nine.

mcq.q: What was Sarai's name changed to?
mcq.explanation: Genesis 17:15 records this.

mcq.q: Which verse says that all peoples on earth will be blessed through Abraham?
mcq.explanation: Genesis 12:3 contains this promise.

mcq.q: What is a patriarch?
options: The father and leader of a family or nation
mcq.explanation: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are called patriarchs.

mcq.q: Which of these shows obedience like Abraham's?
options: Following good instructions even when it is hard
mcq.explanation: Abraham obeyed God without knowing the whole plan.

mcq.q: Abram travelled from Haran to Canaan, which lies to the south-west of Haran. In which direction did he travel?
mcq.explanation: Canaan is south-west of Haran, so he travelled south-west.

mcq.q: What does the word "annunciation" mean?
mcq.explanation: The annunciation is the announcement of Jesus' birth to Mary.

mcq.q: Which angel appeared to Mary?
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:26 says God sent the angel Gabriel.

mcq.q: In which town did Mary live?
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:26 says Gabriel came to Nazareth in Galilee.

mcq.q: To whom was Mary engaged to be married?
mcq.explanation: Mary was engaged to Joseph of the house of David.

mcq.q: What name did the angel tell Mary to give her son?
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:31 says to call Him Jesus.

mcq.q: Who would come upon Mary so that she could conceive?
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:35 says the Holy Spirit would come on her.

mcq.q: What did Mary answer to the angel's message?
options: I am the Lord's servant, may your word to me be fulfilled
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:38 records her humble answer.

mcq.q: Which verse says that nothing is impossible with God?
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:37 is the memory verse of this topic.

mcq.q: Whom did the angel say was expecting a child in old age?
mcq.explanation: Mary's relative Elizabeth was expecting a baby.

mcq.q: Why is the birth of Jesus unique?
options: He was born in a palace
He was conceived by the Holy Spirit
He was born in a rich home
mcq.explanation: Jesus was conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit.

mcq.q: What does the name Jesus mean?
mcq.explanation: Matthew 1:21 links His name to saving people from their sins.

mcq.q: Which quality of Mary should we copy?
mcq.explanation: Mary trusted God and called herself the Lord's servant.

mcq.q: Who was told about the birth of Jesus in a dream?
mcq.explanation: Matthew 1:20 says an angel appeared to Joseph in a dream.

mcq.q: What was Zechariah's job?
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:5 says he was a priest.

mcq.q: Who was John the Baptist's mother?
mcq.explanation: Elizabeth was Zechariah's wife.

mcq.q: Where was Zechariah when the angel appeared to him?
mcq.explanation: He was burning incense in the temple.

mcq.q: What did the angel tell Zechariah to name the baby?
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:13 says his name would be John.

mcq.q: Why could Zechariah not speak for a time?
options: He did not believe the angel's words
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:20 says he would be silent because he did not believe.

mcq.q: How did Zechariah get his speech back?
mcq.explanation: His mouth was opened when he wrote the name.

mcq.q: What was John's main work?
options: Preparing the way for the Lord
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:76 says he would prepare the way.

mcq.q: Which verse in Luke says that John would go before the Lord to prepare His way?
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:76-79 speaks about John's task.

mcq.q: What does "forerunner" mean?
options: One who goes before to prepare
mcq.explanation: A forerunner goes ahead.

mcq.q: What did John call people to do?
mcq.explanation: John called people to turn from their sins.

mcq.q: Where did John preach?
mcq.explanation: John preached in the wilderness by the Jordan.

mcq.q: Which angel appeared to Zechariah?
mcq.explanation: Gabriel said, "I stand in the presence of God."

mcq.q: What kind of life did Zechariah and Elizabeth lead?
mcq.explanation: Luke 1:6 says both were righteous.

mcq.q: Where was Bartimaeus sitting when Jesus passed?
mcq.explanation: Mark 10:46 says he was by the roadside.

mcq.q: What was Bartimaeus' problem?
mcq.explanation: Bartimaeus was a blind beggar.

mcq.q: What did Bartimaeus call Jesus?
mcq.explanation: He called out, "Jesus, Son of David."

mcq.q: What did he ask Jesus for?
mcq.explanation: He asked for mercy and said, "I want to see."

mcq.q: How did the crowd treat him at first?
options: They told him to be quiet
mcq.explanation: Many rebuked him and told him to be quiet.

mcq.q: What did Bartimaeus do when Jesus called him?
options: Threw his cloak aside and jumped up
mcq.explanation: He threw off his cloak and came to Jesus.

mcq.q: What did Jesus say made Bartimaeus well?
mcq.explanation: Jesus said, "Your faith has healed you."

mcq.q: What did Bartimaeus do after he could see?
mcq.explanation: Mark 10:52 says he followed Jesus along the road.

mcq.q: What is a miracle?
options: An amazing act that shows God's power
mcq.explanation: Miracles show God's power.

mcq.q: Which is a kind way to help a blind person?
options: Greet them by name and offer to guide them
mcq.explanation: Kindness and respect help people with disabilities.

mcq.q: Which of these helps to protect our eyes?
options: Not rubbing them with dirty hands
mcq.explanation: Clean hands protect the eyes from infection.

short.q: State two promises that God made to Abram in Genesis 12:1-3.
short.answer: To make him a great nation, to bless him, to make his name great, and to bless all peoples through him.

short.q: Explain why God changed Abram's name to Abraham.
short.answer: God made a covenant with him and promised that he would be a father of many nations. The new name reminded him of this promise.
short.working: 1 mark for the covenant, 1 for the promise, 1 for the name as a reminder.

short.q: Give three ways of obeying God in daily life.
short.answer: Obey parents and teachers, read and follow the Bible, tell the truth, pray, be kind.

short.q: Describe how Abram showed obedience when God called him.
short.answer: He left his country, his people and his father's household. He went to a land he did not know. He took his wife, nephew and belongings. He was seventy-five years old.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid point up to 4.

short.q: Explain how a child can show appreciation for God's blessings, using what you learned about Abraham.
short.answer: Abraham received God's blessings and passed them on. A child can thank God in prayer for family, food, health and school, share with others, obey God, and be a blessing as Abraham was told to be.
short.working: 1 mark for blessings to Abraham, 1 for thanking God, 1 for examples of blessings, 1 for sharing, 1 for obeying or being a blessing.

short.q: State two things the angel Gabriel said about the child that Mary would bear.
short.answer: He will be great, He will be called Son of the Most High, He will have the throne of David, His kingdom will never end. Any two.

short.q: Give two reasons why the birth of Jesus is unique.
short.answer: Conceived by the Holy Spirit, announced by an angel, He is the Son of God and Saviour.

short.q: Describe how Mary responded to the angel's message.
short.answer: She was troubled at first, asked how it could happen since she was a virgin, and then accepted, saying she was the Lord's servant.
short.working: 1 mark for being troubled or asking, 1 for how, 1 for accepting.

short.q: State three qualities of Mary that a child can copy.
short.answer: Trust in God, obedience, humility, purity.

short.q: Write the message of Luke 1:37 in your own words and describe a situation in which it can comfort a child.
short.answer: Nothing is impossible with God. It can comfort a child who is afraid before an exam or when a family member is very sick, because God can help.
short.working: 1 mark for the meaning, 1 for a suitable situation, 2 for explaining how it comforts.

short.q: Explain why sexual purity is important and how children can begin to live a holy life like Mary.
short.answer: The body is a gift from God, and sexual relations are meant for marriage. Purity keeps us safe and honours God. Children can begin by respecting their bodies, avoiding harmful places and media, obeying parents, praying and saying no to wrong.
short.working: 1 mark for body as gift, 1 for marriage, 1 for honouring God, 1 for respecting body or avoiding harm, 1 for a prayer or obedience.

short.q: Who were the parents of John the Baptist?
short.answer: Zechariah and Elizabeth.

short.q: State two things the angel said about John before he was born.
short.answer: He would bring joy, be great before the Lord, be filled with the Holy Spirit, and turn many to God. Any two.

short.q: Explain why Zechariah was unable to speak.
short.answer: He doubted the angel's message. The angel said that he would be silent until the baby was born because he did not believe.
short.working: 1 mark for doubt, 1 for the angel's words, 1 for silence until it happened.

short.q: Give three ways of turning away from sin and living righteously.
short.answer: Say sorry to God; be honest; be kind; obey parents; pray and read the Bible.

short.q: Describe the naming of John.
short.answer: On the eighth day people wanted to call him Zechariah. Elizabeth said his name is John. They asked Zechariah, who wrote, "His name is John." His speech returned and he praised God.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid point up to 4.

short.q: Explain how John the Baptist prepared the way for Jesus and what we can learn about living righteously.
short.answer: John preached in the wilderness, called people to repent and baptised them, so their hearts were ready for Jesus. We can learn to turn away from sin, be honest and kind, pray, and tell others about Jesus by our example.
short.working: 1 mark for preaching, 1 for repentance, 1 for baptism or readiness, 1 for turning from sin, 1 for a righteous example.

short.q: State two ways in which Bartimaeus showed faith in Jesus.
short.answer: He called out to Jesus; he kept shouting when told to be quiet; he came at once; he asked for sight.

short.q: Give two ways of helping a person who is blind.
short.answer: Greet them by name, offer to guide, include them, do not tease.

short.q: Explain what the healing of Bartimaeus teaches about Jesus.
short.answer: Jesus has power over sickness. He cares about the poor and those who suffer. He responds to faith.

short.q: Describe how Jesus responded when Bartimaeus called for mercy.
short.answer: Jesus stopped and said, "Call him." He asked what he wanted, then healed him and told him that his faith had healed him.
short.working: 1 mark for stopping, 1 for asking, 1 for healing.

short.q: Give four ways in which we can care for our eyes and health.
short.answer: Keep hands clean; do not read in dim light; go to the clinic when eyes hurt; eat vegetables and fruit; rest.

short.q: Explain how a child can show faith in God when they or a family member is sick.
short.answer: Pray, believe that God cares, ask trusted adults, go to a clinic or hospital for treatment, thank God for help, and continue to trust. Faith does not mean ignoring doctors.
short.working: 1 mark for prayer, 1 for belief in God's care, 1 for seeking treatment, 1 for thanks, 1 for continuing to trust.

short.q: Why were people with leprosy kept apart in Bible times?
short.answer: The disease was contagious and people feared it would spread.
short.working: 1 mark for disease and 1 for fear of spread.

short.q: Name two ways of expressing thanks to people who are kind to us.
short.answer: Say thank you, write a card, help them in return.

short.q: Describe how the ten lepers showed faith.
short.answer: They called out to Jesus; they obeyed His command to go to the priests before they were healed; one returned to give thanks.

short.q: State three ways of thanking God every day.
short.answer: Pray, sing songs of praise, worship at church, use His gifts well, write a thank-you note.

short.q: Explain what the story teaches about gratitude and give one example from school life.
short.answer: Jesus noticed that only one of the ten returned to thank Him. We should be thankful to God and to people. Example: thanking a teacher who helped with a difficult lesson.
short.working: 1 mark for the lesson, 1 for Jesus noticing, 1 for a school example, 1 for explanation of gratitude.

short.q: Explain how we can prevent the spread of contagious diseases and how we should treat those who are sick.
short.answer: Wash hands with soap, keep the environment clean, eat well, visit the clinic and follow the advice of health workers. We should treat the sick with care, kindness and respect and not reject them, as Jesus did.
short.working: 1 mark for hygiene, 1 for clean environment, 1 for clinic advice, 1 for kindness, 1 for not rejecting the sick.
